title: Settings (SettingsAndHelp)

scenarios.title: Settings applies its documented behavior
scenarios.expected: Settings (BtnSettings) is invoked on the documented fixture deck and produces its documented effect on the selection or presentation, leaves no new entry in %TEMP%\oPenEfficiency\error_YYYYMMDD.log and does not leave PowerPoint or the add-in in an unstable state.

scenarios.title: The icon-colour mode resolves to the documented theme resources and layers
scenarios.expected: FeatureIconColorPolicy resolves the persisted icon-colour mode for every consumer: a disabled icon uses the muted resource in both modes, 'PowerPoint' keeps the neutral base layer and ignores a stored feature colour, accent layers map to their audited semantic resources (create and success green stay independent), and 'Feature colors' hands the stored colour to both layers.

scenarios.title: The comma-delimited settings boundary preserves its legacy token contract
scenarios.expected: DelimitedSettingTokens round-trips the persisted token format: parsing trims entries, drops empty ones and de-duplicates case-insensitively, serialization joins with ', ', hex colours normalize to upper-case six or eight digit tokens and reject invalid input, and font names are trimmed while a comma disqualifies a candidate.

scenarios.title: Acceptance runner arguments bind to the runner's named parameters
scenarios.expected: The acceptance driver parses powershell-script runner arguments into named parameters and splats them as a hashtable (switches bind as true, value lists as lists), and a token that is not a parameter name fails loudly - never a positional array splat, which passes '-Commands' as a literal value and makes the runner's parameter binder reject it. The host-free pin AcceptanceRunnerArgumentsBindByName reddens on the positional splat.

scenarios.title: PowerPoint startup recovers from a stale debug add-in registration
scenarios.expected: On the real PowerPoint host a baseline start completes add-in startup; pointing the registration at a stale bin\Debug manifest degrades startup (no add-in startup log within the observation window, or a load penalty above 2.5x the healthy baseline); the canonical reset restores the Release manifest with LoadBehavior=3 and a subsequent host start completes startup again. The run records healthy-before, the degraded stale phase, registry recovery and healthy-after as evidence.

scenarios.title: The deployment identity gate normalizes build-stamp version components
scenarios.expected: A build stamp with a zero-padded hour component (yyyy.M.d.HHmm, e.g. 2026.9.28.0020) equals its read-back System.Version after normalization, so the canonical checkpoint passes at any time of day, while a genuinely different identity still fails. The host-free test BuildStampIdentityComparisonNormalizesVersionComponents pins the normalized comparison.

scenarios.title: Settings ComboBoxes use the themed template
scenarios.expected: Every Settings ComboBox (including Anchor Object) uses the themed template for closed field, popup surface, arrow area, ComboBoxItem rows and selected/focused states in Light and Dark mode.
ownerSteps: Open Settings and inspect the Anchor Object ComboBox in Light mode: no native/system chrome.
Switch to Dark mode and confirm the ComboBox, its popup and item rows follow the theme.
Open the dropdown and check hover/focus states on the rows.

scenarios.title: Changing the application theme never terminates powerpnt.exe
scenarios.expected: Applying a different theme while a shown window owns a HWND mutates neither AllowsTransparency nor WindowStyle; the WPF invalidation of the window style never throws System.InvalidOperationException and the host survives. The office leg opens the Settings dialog, swaps Light/Dark on the UI thread, and closes it: PASS means windowObserved=True, themeSwapped=True, survived=True with zero new error-log entries.

scenarios.title: Sidebar follows live Light/Dark theme switching
scenarios.expected: Switching the application theme to Dark updates the live Sidebar tree and its dynamically created controls immediately; a persisted appearance value never overrides the selected theme.
ownerSteps: Open the Sidebar, switch the application theme from Settings to Dark and confirm the live tree re-renders immediately.
Switch back to Light and confirm the same immediate re-render.
Set a custom background, switch themes and confirm the custom background persists while theme-tracking surfaces follow the theme.

scenarios.title: Sidebar window commands open their windows
scenarios.expected: A Sidebar command that is expected to open UI either opens the window (activating an already-open one) or reports a user-visible failure; it never ends as a silent no-op. The office leg proves the open half for BtnSettings and BtnExploreFeatures on a real host.

scenarios.title: Installer builds keep the committed release identity across nested builds
scenarios.expected: An installer build stamps the committed release CalVer and every nested build it starts (feature-acceptance runner projects) reuses that identity mode instead of re-stamping the deployment manifests with the per-build stamp, so the deployment identity gate validates exactly the identity Office will load. The host-free test InstallerIdentityModeReachesNestedBuilds pins the hand-off.
